hook.situation: Your team has a deadline today. You cannot cancel, you do not believe anyone will give up, and only one realistic method remains.
objectives: Use -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 for a no-choice situation.
Use -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 to strongly reject a possibility.
Use -(으)ㄹ 뿐이다 or N뿐이다 to limit the situation to only one action or option.
hook.whyItMatters: English learners often say 'I can't' when they mean 'I have no choice but to.' Korean separates inability, inevitability, disbelief, and only-option nuance very clearly.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 — to have no choice but to
grammarNotes.func: Use this to say there's no other option, so you end up doing the action whether you want to or not. It often sounds a little reluctant: "There's nothing else I can do, so I just do this."

formTable.when: Verb stem ends in a consonant (받침 O)
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹을 수밖에 없다 (have no choice but to eat)

formTable.when: Verb stem ends in a vowel (받침 X)
formTable.ex: 가다 → 갈 수밖에 없다 (have no choice but to go)

formTable.when: Verb stem ends in ㄹ (ㄹ stays, just add 수밖에 없다)
formTable.ex: 살다 → 살 수밖에 없다 (have no choice but to live)

formTable.when: Adjectives work too (= it can only be / it's bound to be)
formTable.ex: 비싸다 → 비쌀 수밖에 없다 (it's bound to be expensive)

examples.en: There was no bus, so I had no choice but to walk.
examples.note: A reason clause (없어서) plus this pattern is the most common shape: cause, then forced result.

examples.ko: 시간이 없어서 택시를 탈 수밖에 없어요.
examples.romanization: sigani eopseoseo taeksi-reul tal su-bakke eopseoyo.
examples.en: I don't have time, so I have no choice but to take a taxi.
examples.note: 탈 from 타다 (vowel stem) just adds -ㄹ. Shows the everyday 'I'm forced into it' feeling.

examples.ko: 친구가 약속을 안 지켜서 화가 날 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.romanization: chinguga yaksogeul an jikyeoseo hwaga nal su-bakke eopseosseoyo.
examples.en: My friend broke our plans, so I couldn't help getting angry.
examples.note: With feelings it means 'can't help but'. Getting angry was the only natural reaction.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 음식이 맛있어서 사람이 많을 수밖에 없어요.
examples.romanization: i sikdangeun eumsigi masisseoseo sarami manheul su-bakke eopseoyo.
examples.en: This place's food is so good, of course it's packed.
examples.note: With an adjective (많다) it means 'it's bound to be'. A natural, can't-be-otherwise conclusion.

keyPoint.label: 수밖에 없다 vs. -아/어야 하다
keyPoint.body: -아/어야 하다 means you 'have to / should' do something (a duty, but other choices might still exist). V-(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 means every other option is gone, so you do it even if you'd rather not. '공부해야 해요' = I should study; '공부할 수밖에 없어요' = I've got no other choice but to study. (You'll meet -아/어야 하다 in its own lesson.)

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 수밖에 sounds like [수바께]: the ㄲ of 밖 links into 에 and stays tense. So 수밖에 없다 comes out as [수바께 업따].

drill.instruction: Because of the reason, only one thing is left to do. Answer with V-(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없어요.
drill.model: 비가 와요. (집에 있다) → 비가 와서 집에 있을 수밖에 없어요.
items: 돈이 없어요. (집에서 밥을 먹다) → 돈이 없어서 집에서 밥을 ____.
길이 막혀요. (지하철을 타다) → 길이 막혀서 지하철을 ____.
숙제가 많아요. (집에 늦게까지 있다) → 숙제가 많아서 집에 늦게까지 ____.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 밖에 ('other than / except') always pairs with a negative, so the ending is always 없다, never 있다. 'There's nothing other than walking' = 없다. Saying 있어요 here flips the meaning and just sounds broken to a Korean ear.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 — there's no way that's true
grammarNotes.func: Use this to say you really don't believe something: you're sure it can't be the case because it makes no sense. It's the Korean way of saying "There's no way…" or "It can't possibly be that…"

formTable.when: Verb/Adjective stem ends in a consonant (받침 O)
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹을 리가 없다 (there's no way he'd eat it)

formTable.when: Verb/Adjective stem ends in a vowel (받침 X)
formTable.ex: 오다 → 올 리가 없다 (there's no way it'll come / he'll come)
가다 → 갔을 리가 없다 (there's no way he went)
학생 → 학생일 리가 없다 (there's no way he's a student)

examples.ko: 그 친구가 거짓말을 했을 리가 없어요.
examples.romanization: geu chinguga geojinmareul haesseul liga eopseoyo.
examples.en: There's no way that friend lied.
examples.note: Past form 했을 리가 없다 rejects that a past action happened. Very common with 거짓말.

examples.ko: 지금 밤 12시인데 학생들이 학교에 있을 리가 없어요.
examples.romanization: jigeum bam yeoldu-si-inde haksaengdeuri hakgyo-e isseul liga eopseoyo.
examples.en: It's midnight now, so there's no way the students are at school.
examples.note: A known fact (it's the middle of the night) makes the idea impossible. The typical 'fact + 리가 없다' shape.

examples.ko: 한국어를 배운 지 일주일밖에 안 됐는데 잘할 리가 없어요.
examples.romanization: hangugeo-reul baeun ji iljuilbakke an dwaenneunde jalhal liga eopseoyo.
examples.en: He's only been learning Korean for a week, so there's no way he's good at it.
examples.note: Often follows a reason clause with -는데. Uses 잘하다, an everyday verb.

examples.ko: 이 책이 만 원이라고요? 그렇게 쌀 리가 없어요.
examples.romanization: i chaegi man wonira-goyo? geureoke ssal liga eopseoyo.
examples.en: This book is 10,000 won? There's no way it's that cheap.
examples.note: Adjective 싸다 works too. The speaker rejects the claim as impossible, not just unlikely.

keyPoint.label: -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 vs. -(으)ㄹ 수 없다
keyPoint.body: -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 is about real ability: 'can't do it' (갈 수 없어요 = I'm not able to go). -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 is about your certainty that a claim is false: 'there's no way that's true' (갔을 리가 없어요 = no way he went). The first is about being able; the second is about believing.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 없어요 sounds like [업써요]: the ㅅ of the 없- cluster slides onto the next syllable and goes tense, while ㅂ stays as a stop. So 리가 없어요 comes out as [리가 업써요].

drill.instruction: You don't believe the statement. Reject it with V-(으)ㄹ 리가 없어요.
drill.model: 민수가 시험에 떨어졌어요. → 민수가 시험에 떨어졌을 리가 없어요.
items: 저 사람이 한국 사람이에요. → 저 사람이 한국 사람일 리가 ____.
동생이 벌써 집에 갔어요. → 동생이 벌써 집에 ____ 리가 없어요.
이 영화가 재미없어요. → 이 영화가 재미____ 리가 없어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 저는 오늘 갈 리가 없어요. (meaning: I can't go today)
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 저는 오늘 못 가요. / 갈 수 없어요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'there's no way' covers both 'I'm unable to' and 'I don't believe it.' But 리가 없다 only means disbelief about a fact, and it sounds odd about your own plans. For 'I can't go,' use 못 가요 or 갈 수 없어요. Save 갈 리가 없어요 for 'there's no way he'd go.'

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄹ 뿐이다 / N뿐이다 — only, nothing more
grammarNotes.func: Use this to limit things to just one: 'that's all there is, nothing else.' With verbs/adjectives it means 'only does / is only'; attached straight to a noun, 뿐이다 means 'only that, and nothing else.'

formTable.ex: 믿다 → 믿을 뿐이다 (I just believe it, that's all)
하다 → 했을 뿐이다 (I just did it, nothing more)

formTable.when: Noun (no -(으)ㄹ; 뿐 attaches straight to the noun)

examples.en: I only told the truth, that's all.
examples.note: Past 말했을 뿐이다 is the classic 'I just did X, so don't blame me' use.

examples.en: I was just joking, nothing more. Don't be mad.
examples.note: 그냥 ('just') goes naturally with 뿐이다 to play an action down.

examples.en: Right now there's only water in the fridge.
examples.note: Noun case: 뿐 attaches straight to 물 (no -(으)ㄹ). Means 'water and nothing else.'

examples.en: In this neighborhood, Minsu is my only friend.
examples.note: N뿐이다 with a person noun (민수) = 'only him, no one else.' Very common in speech.

keyPoint.label: -(으)ㄹ 뿐이다 vs. N뿐이다 (and 만)
keyPoint.body: After a verb or adjective, use the -(으)ㄹ form: 기다릴 뿐이에요. After a noun, drop -(으)ㄹ and stick 뿐 right on: 물뿐이에요. Compare 만 ('only'): 만 picks one out of several options (물만 마셔요 = I drink only water), while N뿐이다 says that noun is all there is (물뿐이에요 = water is all there is).

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 뿐이에요 links smoothly as [뿌니에요]: the ㄴ of 뿐 slides onto 이. With a noun like 물, 물뿐이에요 sounds like [물뿌니에요].

drill.instruction: Say it's only this, nothing more. Answer with -(으)ㄹ 뿐이에요 for verbs/adjectives, or N뿐이에요 for nouns.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: After a noun, 뿐 attaches directly with no -(으)ㄹ: 물뿐이에요, 저뿐이에요. The -(으)ㄹ 뿐이다 form is only for verbs and adjectives (기다릴 뿐이에요). English speakers tend to glue an extra ending on before 뿐 with nouns, but the noun just takes 뿐 by itself.

extendedVocabulary.english: to have no choice but to

exampleSentence.en: The deadline is today, so we have no choice but to work late.
exampleSentence.note: No-choice situation caused by a real constraint.

exampleSentence.en: There is no way we would give up now.
exampleSentence.note: Strong disbelief, not a soft guess.

exampleSentence.en: The only thing left is this method.
exampleSentence.note: Limits the situation to one option.

exampleSentence.en: If the deadline is today, it cannot be helped.
The deadline is today, so there are not many choices.
exampleSentence.note: The pressure that creates the no-choice frame.

exampleSentence.en: Today I have no choice but to work late.
There is no way we would give up now.
The only thing left is this method.
With the current method, it is almost impossible.

exampleSentence.ko: 이런 상황에서는 다시 확인할 수밖에 없어요.
exampleSentence.en: In this situation, we have no choice but to check again.
exampleSentence.note: The noun that explains why there is no other option.

exampleSentence.en: There is no way the data is wrong.
exampleSentence.note: Work/study content that can be checked or revised.

exampleSentence.en: We have no choice but to rewrite the explanation.
exampleSentence.note: A realistic repair action under a deadline.

extendedDialogue.setting: A team handles a deadline where there is no realistic choice left.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: The deadline is today, so we have no choice but to work late.
lines.grammarNote: -ㄹ 수밖에 없다 shows the situation leaves no other option.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Still, there is no way we would give up now.
lines.grammarNote: -ㄹ 리가 없다 strongly rejects a possibility.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 자료는 맞지만 설명은 다시 쓸 수밖에 없어요.
lines.romanization: jaryoneun matjiman seolmyeongeun dasi sseul subakke eopseoyo.
lines.en: The data is right, but we have no choice but to rewrite the explanation.
lines.grammarNote: The no-choice frame fits a specific next action.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: In the end, this method is the only thing left.
lines.grammarNote: N뿐이다 limits the remaining option to one thing.

readingText.title: 마감이라서 할 수밖에 없어요
readingText.body: 마감이 가까우면 선택지가 줄어들어요. 이때 '할 수 없어요'라고 말하면 능력이 없거나 불가능하다는 뜻이 되지만, '할 수밖에 없어요'라고 말하면 하기 싫어도 그 방법밖에 없다는 뜻이 돼요. 반대로 '포기할 리가 없어요'는 포기할 가능성을 강하게 부정하는 말이에요. 그리고 '남은 건 이 방법뿐이에요'는 다른 선택이 없고 이 방법만 남았다는 뜻이에요. 세 표현은 모두 한계와 관련이 있지만, 각각 no choice, no way, only one이라는 다른 느낌을 가지고 있어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: When a deadline is close, choices shrink. 할 수밖에 없어요 means there is no choice but to do it, not that you cannot do it. 리가 없어요 strongly rejects a possibility, and 뿐이에요 limits the situation to only one remaining option.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 할 수 없어요와 할 수밖에 없어요는 어떻게 달라요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 할 수 없어요는 불가능, 할 수밖에 없어요는 다른 선택이 없다는 뜻이에요.

culturalNote.title: No Choice, No Way, Only
culturalNote.body: Korean often separates the speaker's attitude from the facts of the situation. 수밖에 없다 sounds resigned to a constraint, 리가 없다 sounds confident or emotionally certain, and 뿐이다 sounds limiting or modest.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing the pattern, label the meaning in English: no choice, no way, or only.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence means “I have no choice but to work late”?
inlineExercises.explanation: 수밖에 없다 means the situation leaves no other option.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence strongly rejects a possibility?
inlineExercises.explanation: -ㄹ 리가 없다 means there is no way that possibility is true.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence means only one method remains?
options: 남은 건 이 방법일 리가 없어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: N뿐이다 limits the situation to only that noun.

inlineExercises.prompt: 마감___ 있어서 야근할 수밖에 없어요. (Because there is a deadline...)
inlineExercises.explanation: 있다 takes 이/가 for the thing that exists. 마감이 있어서 gives the reason before the no-choice result.
-(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없어요 means there is no choice but to do it. 야근하다 becomes 야근할 수밖에 없어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'There is no way that person will give up.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ 리가 없어요 strongly rejects a possibility. 포기할 리가 없어요 means giving up is not plausible.
뿐이에요 limits the situation to only one thing. 방법은 sets the topic as the available method.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: '그 사람이 포기할 리가 있어요.' (intended: no way)
inlineExercises.explanation: The “no way” pattern needs 리가 없어요. 리가 있어요 does not express strong rejection.

inlineExercises.prompt: Only one realistic option remains. Which sentence fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: 뿐이에요 means only this and nothing more. The other options compare or guess rather than limit the options.
어쩔 수 없죠 is the fixed phrase for accepting a no-choice situation. It fits when the speaker cannot change the circumstances.

bullets: -ㄹ 수밖에 없다 = no choice but to do it.
-ㄹ 리가 없다 = there is no way that is true.
-뿐이다 = only this action, role, or option.
Do not confuse 할 수 없어요 with 할 수밖에 없어요.

writingTask.prompt: Reply to a friend who invited you out tonight: explain that you have no choice but to work late, and that there's no way you'll finish early.
writingTask.hint: Use -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 for 'no choice but to' (야근할 수밖에 없어요), -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 for 'no way' (일찍 끝날 리가 없어요), and -(으)ㄹ 뿐이다 / N뿐이다 for 'only' (방법이 이것뿐이에요).
writingTask.model: 미안해요, 오늘은 마감이라서 야근할 수밖에 없어요. 일이 너무 많아서 일찍 끝날 리가 없어요. 지금은 그냥 열심히 하는 수밖에 없죠. 방법이 이것뿐이에요.
writingTask.modelEn: Sorry, today is the deadline, so I have no choice but to work late. There's so much work that there's no way it'll finish early. For now I just have no choice but to work hard. This is the only way.

canDo: Say I have no other option with -(으)ㄹ 수밖에 없다 (야근할 수밖에 없어요)
Reject something as impossible with -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 (끝날 리가 없어요)
Limit things to just one with -(으)ㄹ 뿐이다 / N뿐이다 (이것뿐이에요)
Sound resigned about a fixed situation (어쩔 수 없죠, 마감)
